title: 1914 Train station platform, sending off the troops WWI
description: In 1914, citizens of Hartland gathered at the train station to bid farewell to the 67th Regiment and Brighton Engineers as they departed for World War I. The troops left Woodstock for training in Quebec before heading to the front lines. At the decorated Hartland station, two carloads of soldiers were greeted by waving flags and the sound of a band playing “God Save the King” as the train arrived. When it departed, few eyes remained dry, knowing that many would not return.
